summary: AURA: Echo Squad is an all-ages, 2-player cooperative climate strategy game designed to turn abstract space mission trade-offs into an engaging, interactive simulation. Created by twin sisters, the game features both Online Co-Op and Offline Solo modes with AI companions. Players dynamically balance three specialized roles—Eco-Engineer, NASA Analyst, and Climate Diplomat—to manage limited energy, mass, and financial budgets while defending Earth's atmosphere from Global Warming, Polar Ice Melting, and Wildfires. By integrating real-source open NASA satellite telemetry (OCO-3, ICESat-2, and MODIS) into live visual alerts and science charts, AURA empowers players to understand how engineering decisions directly impact planetary defense and environmental sustainability.
details:
Project Functionality & Gameplay:

AURA: Echo Squad is a 2-player cooperative strategy game designed for all ages, supporting both Online Co-Op and Offline Solo modes with AI companions. Players manage three specialized roles—Eco-Engineer, NASA Analyst, and Climate Diplomat—to balance limited energy, mass, and financial budgets while defending Earth's atmosphere across 10 progressive levels covering Global Warming, Polar Ice Melting, and Wildfires.

Benefits & Impact:

The game transforms abstract space mission trade-offs and complex NASA satellite data (OCO-3, ICESat-2, and MODIS) into live, interactive visual alerts and science charts. This empowers students and families to understand how engineering decisions directly impact planetary defense and environmental sustainability.

Tools & Technologies Used:

We utilized Figma for UI/UX wireframing and brand identity guidelines, AI image generation tools for semi-realistic vector avatars and environments, CapCut for visual rendering, and iLovePDF/Google Drive for final presentation structuring.

Creativity & Team Factors:

Developed by twin sisters (Team Aura Pioneers), our natural synergy inspired the 2-player cooperative mechanic. We prioritized accessibility (all-ages, online/offline flexibility) and a cohesive neon sci-fi HUD aesthetic to make climate science engaging and intuitive.
